shared_elements: anthropomorphic figure carved in low relief on a large upright block
schematic head/face at the top of the block
concentric circle or disc motif on the body
curving arc lines defining shoulders/arms across the body
row of short parallel incised strokes (comb-like/ribbed band)
frontal, symmetrical, whole-body composition filling the stone
justification: Both show a frontal, symmetrical anthropomorphic figure rendered in shallow relief over the whole face of an upright block, with a schematic head above, curving arc lines marking shoulders/arms, a concentric-circle disc on the torso, and a band of short parallel strokes; this combination of low-relief body markings on a monolithic figure is fairly specific. The differences are in emphasis and detail: A's head is a large flat-topped rectangular block with a distinct browline and fine incised patterning above, its disc is centrally placed on the chest with paired arcs and horizontal bands below, whereas B's head is a small rounded loop-like element with the comb-like strokes hanging directly below it and long tapering limb lines running down the sides, giving a looser and more attenuated figure.
